items.question: During a CAT A clearway take-off, an engine fails before TDP. What is the correct action?
options: Reject take-off and land back on the helipad/runway
Maintain V2 speed and climb away
items.explanation: In a CAT A clearway take-off, if engine failure occurs before TDP, the pilot must reject the take-off and land back.

items.question: In a CAT A rejected landing (before LDP), the procedure is to:
options: Initiate go-around or balked landing profile
items.explanation: If engine failure occurs before LDP during CAT A landing, pilot must perform balked landing/go-around.

items.question: During CAT A take-off with a defined clearway, which factor must be considered for TDP determination?
options: Height of obstacles in departure path
items.explanation: Obstacle clearance is critical for determining TDP in a CAT A clearway take-off.

items.question: In CAT A landing profile, the rejected landing distance must account for:
options: Obstacle clearance and transition to balked landing
items.explanation: Rejected landing distance includes obstacle clearance and balked landing path requirements.

items.question: When both engines fail after TDP in CAT A take-off, what is the procedure?
items.explanation: If both engines fail after TDP, autorotation is required.

items.question: What defines the LDP (Landing Decision Point)?
options: Last point to safely reject landing and perform go-around
First point where V2 speed is achieved
Altitude where collective is reduced to idle
items.explanation: The LDP is the last point where the pilot can decide to reject landing and initiate balked landing/go-around.

items.question: During CAT A vertical take-off, if engine failure occurs before TDP:
options: Land back and do not continue take-off
items.explanation: For CAT A vertical take-off, an engine failure before TDP requires landing back.

items.question: For a CAT A balked landing, what minimum climb gradient must be ensured OEI?
items.explanation: CAT A balked landing requires an OEI climb gradient of 3.3%.

items.question: What is the purpose of TDP (Take-off Decision Point)?
options: Point to decide continue or reject take-off after engine failure
items.explanation: TDP defines the decision point to either reject or continue the take-off in case of engine failure.

items.question: CAT A landing requires the approach path to be clear of obstacles up to:
items.explanation: In CAT A landing, obstacle clearance must be assured until the LDP.

items.question: During CAT A vertical take-off in confined area, why is hover height limited?
options: To minimize exposure time to engine failure before TDP
items.explanation: Limiting hover height reduces exposure time to engine failure before reaching TDP.

items.question: What is V2 in CAT A operations?
options: Minimum speed providing required climb gradient OEI
items.explanation: V2 ensures the minimum speed providing the necessary climb gradient in OEI conditions.

items.question: In CAT A landing profile, if an engine fails before LDP:
items.explanation: If an engine fails before LDP, the pilot must reject landing and execute OEI climb away.

items.question: What is the minimum height and speed at the Initial Point (IP) in a CAT A profile?
items.explanation: The IP is defined at 300 ft and 70 kt in CAT A profiles.

items.question: Which speed must be reached and maintained after TDP in CAT A take-off?
items.explanation: After TDP, the helicopter must accelerate to and maintain Vtoss.

items.question: What is Vy (all engines operative best rate of climb)?
items.explanation: Vy for AW169 is 75 kt, giving best rate of climb with both engines operative.

items.question: What must be ensured before reaching LDP during CAT A landing?
items.explanation: Before reaching LDP, configuration and approach stability must be ensured.

items.question: If engine failure occurs after passing LDP in CAT A landing, what is the procedure?
items.explanation: After LDP, the landing must be continued regardless of engine status.

items.question: Why is the Initial Point (IP) defined in CAT A procedures?
options: To standardize transition from approach to landing
To provide a defined point for balked landing
items.explanation: The IP standardizes the transition point from approach to landing in CAT A procedures.

items.question: During a CAT A vertical landing, what must be assured before LDP?
options: Helicopter in correct configuration and OEI path available
items.explanation: Before LDP, correct landing configuration and an OEI contingency path must be available.

items.question: What is required when an operating limitation is exceeded?
options: No action if the exceedance is short
An entry in the logbook with details of the exceedance
items.explanation: Each exceedance must be recorded in the logbook with which limit was exceeded, duration, and extreme value attained.

items.question: During engine start, which condition requires an aborted engine start?
options: ITT increases beyond engine limits with HOT START caution illuminated
NR remains at zero during start
GEN 1 does not come on line
items.explanation: ITT exceedance with HOT START caution is a trigger to abort the start.

items.question: According to the aborted engine start procedure, what is the first action?
options: Set ENG MODE knob to OFF
items.explanation: Procedure calls to set ENG MODE knob OFF before other actions.

items.question: In the motoring procedure, which cycle is listed?
items.explanation: One of the listed cycles is 30 s ON, 5 min OFF.

items.question: At which NG value should the engine starter be disengaged?
items.explanation: Starter is disengaged by about 54% NG.

items.question: When starting engine 2 (or engine 1 in MAIN drive), NF and NR should begin raising within approximately:
options: 15 seconds above 0 °C, 20 seconds at or below 0 °C
items.explanation: NF/NR should rise within ~15 s (OAT > 0 °C) or ~20 s (OAT ≤ 0 °C).

items.question: Which timing is listed as a trigger for an aborted engine start?
options: No light up within 10 seconds of ENG MODE knob to IDLE
No light up within 20 seconds after ENG MODE knob to OFF
No light up within 5 seconds after CRANK switch
No light up within 30 seconds after IGN legend
items.explanation: No light up within 10 s of ENG MODE knob to IDLE is listed.

items.question: On ground, after an aborted starting procedure, what must be done before motoring or re-starting?
items.explanation: Electrical power must be switched off completely before motoring or re-starting.

items.question: How many times can the chosen motoring cycle be repeated?
items.explanation: The chosen cycle can be repeated 3 times.

items.question: If further motoring is requested beyond the allowed repeats, what rest time is necessary?
items.explanation: A 30 minutes rest time is necessary before further motoring.

items.question: What NG condition prevents the DC generator from coming On Line when selected ON?
items.explanation: If an engine is running at NG lower than ~64%, the DC generator will not come On Line when selected ON.

items.question: What must be done with the PARK BRAKE handle before taxi?
items.explanation: PARK BRAKE handle must be turned to release before taxi.

items.question: What advisory message must clear when releasing the PARK BRAKE?
items.explanation: PARK BRK ON advisory must clear when brake is released.

items.question: How should turning during taxi be performed?
options: With aft cyclic and high collective
With minimum pitch, cyclic central or adjusted for crosswind
items.explanation: Turning whilst taxiing: collective at minimum pitch, cyclic central/adjusted for crosswind.

items.question: What action is prohibited during taxi to slow the aircraft?
items.explanation: Do not use aft cyclic to slow the aircraft.

items.question: What position should both ENG MODE knobs be in for take-off?
items.explanation: Pre Take-Off Checks: ENG MODE knobs must be set to FLT.
references: AW169 QRH Pre Take-Off Checks p.152

items.question: What does pressing the AEO LIM SEL pushbutton do?
options: Limits AEO total torque to 222% TQ
items.explanation: With AEO LIM SEL enabled, AEO torque is limited to 222% TQ.
references: AW169 QRH Pre Take-Off Checks p.152

items.question: With AEO LIM SEL enabled, what advisory is displayed?
items.explanation: Advisory displayed is TQ LIM SEL.
references: AW169 QRH Pre Take-Off Checks p.152

items.question: What is the Take-Off Safety Speed (VTOSS) for the AW169?
items.explanation: VTOSS is 45 KIAS.
references: AW169 QRH Category A Take-Off p.155

items.question: What is the minimum Continued Take-Off Height during CTO?
items.explanation: Minimum CTO height is 15 ft ATS.
references: AW169 QRH Category A Take-Off p.155

items.question: During hover before Category A Take-Off, what hover height should be established?
items.explanation: Establish a 6 ft (1.8 m) hover.
references: AW169 QRH Category A Take-Off p.156

items.question: At Take-Off Decision Point, what is the required pitch input?
items.explanation: At TDP: rotate in 2 sec, 15° nose down relative to hover attitude.
references: AW169 QRH Category A Take-Off p.156

items.question: Passing through VTOSS (45 KIAS), what should be the next step?
items.explanation: Passing VTOSS, continue acceleration to Vy.
references: AW169 QRH Category A Take-Off p.156

items.question: At what altitude should climb be continued to after passing VTOSS?
items.explanation: Continue climb to 1000 ft (300 m) ATS.
references: AW169 QRH Category A Take-Off p.156

items.question: What is the Take-Off Decision Point Height (TDP) for Clear Area Take-Off?
items.explanation: TDP height is 20 ft ATS.
references: AW169 QRH Clear Area Take-Off p.157

items.question: What is the airspeed at TDP for Clear Area Take-Off?
items.explanation: Airspeed at TDP is 20 KIAS.
references: AW169 QRH Clear Area Take-Off p.157

items.question: During Clear Area Take-Off, what must be confirmed with the PARK BRAKE before liftoff?
options: PARK BRK ON advisory is illuminated
PARK BRK ON advisory is not illuminated
PARK BRK FAIL warning is cleared
items.explanation: Confirm PARK BRK ON advisory is not illuminated before liftoff.
references: AW169 QRH Clear Area Take-Off p.157

items.question: During hover for Clear Area Take-Off, what pitch adjustment is required?
items.explanation: Apply cyclic to rotate 10° nose down.
references: AW169 QRH Clear Area Take-Off p.158

items.question: What type of take-off is prohibited according to Offshore and Elevated Helideck Take-Off Procedures?
items.explanation: Take-Off with tail wind component is prohibited.
references: AW169 QRH Offshore/Elevated Helideck Take-Off Procedures p.161

items.question: How much of the wind component increase may the pilot credit, unless otherwise authorized?
items.explanation: Unless otherwise authorized, no more than 50% of the wind component performance increase can be credited.
references: AW169 QRH Offshore/Elevated Helideck Take-Off Procedures p.161

items.question: What is the Take-Off Decision Point Height (TDP) for Offshore/Elevated Helideck procedures?
items.explanation: TDP is 25 ft ATS for Offshore/Elevated Helideck take-off.
references: AW169 QRH Offshore/Elevated Helideck Take-Off Procedures p.161

items.question: In the Wind Benefit Envelope, what wind direction sector provides full wind benefit?
items.explanation: Full wind benefit occurs in the headwind sector 0° ± 10°.

items.question: According to the Wind Limitations chart, at which directions is there no wind benefit?
items.explanation: No wind benefit at crosswind directions 90° and 270°.

items.question: What hover height must be established before Offshore/Elevated Helideck Take-Off?
items.explanation: Establish a 5 ft (1.5 m) hover.
references: AW169 QRH Offshore/Elevated Helideck Take-Off p.163-164

items.question: Where should the nose wheel be positioned in hover during Offshore/Elevated Helideck procedure?
items.explanation: Nose wheel approximately 2 m from the forward edge of the helideck.
references: AW169 QRH Offshore/Elevated Helideck Take-Off p.163

items.question: What vertical climb rate should be used during Offshore/Elevated Helideck Take-Off?
items.explanation: Vertical climb of 400 fpm.
references: AW169 QRH Offshore/Elevated Helideck Take-Off p.163

items.question: At Take-Off Decision Point (TDP) 25 ft ATS during Offshore/Elevated Helideck Take-Off, what pitch attitude is required?
items.explanation: At 25 ft ATS, pitch attitude should be 12° nose down.
references: AW169 QRH Offshore/Elevated Helideck Take-Off p.163-164

items.question: During Offshore/Elevated Helideck Take-Off, after passing 15 kts ground speed, what pitch adjustment must be made?
items.explanation: After reaching 15 kts GS, rotate to 6° nose up.
references: AW169 QRH Offshore/Elevated Helideck Take-Off p.164

items.question: During Offshore/Elevated Helideck Pre Take-Off procedure, how should the PARK BRAKE be applied and confirmed?
options: Ensure PARK BRK FAIL warning is cleared
Apply brake, confirm pressure on pedals, and PARK BRK ON advisory illuminated
Ensure PARK BRK ON extinguished immediately
Move brake lever to neutral without CAS indication
items.explanation: Apply brake, confirm pedal pressure, and PARK BRK ON illuminated on CAS.
references: AW169 QRH Offshore/Elevated Helideck Take-Off p.163

items.question: What NR/NF value must be confirmed prior to Offshore/Elevated Helideck Take-Off?
items.explanation: NF/NR must be confirmed at 103%.
references: AW169 QRH Offshore/Elevated Helideck Take-Off p.163

items.question: Which PFD menu selection is required during Offshore/Elevated Helideck pre-take-off checks?
items.explanation: Select DG on Rig for Offshore/Elevated Helideck operation.
references: AW169 QRH Offshore/Elevated Helideck Take-Off p.163

items.question: During Offshore/Elevated Helideck lift-off, how much PI increase should be applied in approximately 2 seconds?
items.explanation: Increase PI by 15% in approximately 2 seconds.
references: AW169 QRH Offshore/Elevated Helideck Take-Off p.164

items.question: What climb target speed should be reached after Offshore/Elevated Helideck Take-Off?
items.explanation: Climb to Vy = 75 KIAS.
references: AW169 QRH Offshore/Elevated Helideck Take-Off p.164

items.question: If the helicopter is parked outside with OAT at or below –20 °C, what must be done with the batteries?
options: Remove both Main and Auxiliary batteries and store in a heated room
items.explanation: When OAT ≤ –20 °C, both Main and Auxiliary batteries must be removed and stored in a heated room.
references: AW169 QRH Cold Weather Operation p.123

items.question: When can the aircraft be considered NOT COLD SOAKED?
options: Exposed between –20 °C and –40 °C for less than 30 minutes
Exposed below –20 °C for more than 1 hour
Exposed between –10 °C and –20 °C for more than 2 hours
items.explanation: Specific exposure conditions define when the aircraft is NOT COLD SOAKED.
references: AW169 QRH Cold Weather Operation p.123

items.question: What may occur during engine start when using aircraft batteries after cold soak?
options: HOT START caution illumination with automatic abort
items.explanation: Automatic abort and HOT START caution illumination may occur when starting with aircraft batteries after cold soak.
references: AW169 QRH Cold Weather Operation p.123

items.question: During cold start, what is the temporary maximum value the MGB oil pressure may reach?
items.explanation: During cold starting the MGB oil pressure could temporarily reach 6.7 bar (0.7 bar above normal).
references: AW169 QRH Cold Weather Operation p.124
